examples: The weather is cloudy so I feel down.
When I hear good music my mood lifts.
nuance: 기분 means how you feel inside at the moment, your emotional mood. Koreans say 기분이 좋다 or 기분이 나쁘다, always pairing it with 이 as the subject.
mistakes: Saying 기분을 좋아요 instead of 기분이 좋아요

examples: A good idea came to me.
I often think of my family.
In my opinion this is better.
nuance: 생각 means a thought or idea in your head. With 하다 it becomes 생각하다 meaning to think, and 생각이 나다 means something comes to mind.
mistakes: Saying 생각이 해요 instead of 생각을 해요

examples: That person has a warm heart.
I opened my heart to my friend.
nuance: 마음 means the heart or mind as the seat of feelings and intentions, not the physical organ. The idiom 마음에 들다 means to like something.
mistakes: Using 마음 for the physical heart instead of 심장

examples: Last night I had a good dream.
Someday I want to achieve my dream.
nuance: 꿈 means both a dream during sleep and a hope or goal for the future. The natural verb is 꿈을 꾸다 for dreaming and 꿈을 이루다 for achieving.
mistakes: Saying 꿈을 해요 instead of 꿈을 꿔요

examples: I love my family a lot.
I fell in love with that person.
My parents love is really big.
nuance: 사랑 means love in a broad sense, for family, friends, or a partner. With 하다 it becomes the verb 사랑하다, and 사랑에 빠지다 means to fall in love.
mistakes: Saying 사랑이 해요 instead of 사랑을 해요

examples: These days I have many worries.
My mom worries about my health.
Do not worry. It is fine.
nuance: 걱정 means worry or concern about something uncertain. With 하다 it becomes 걱정하다, and 걱정하지 마요 is a common way to comfort someone.
mistakes: Saying 걱정이 해요 instead of 걱정을 해요

nuance: 문제 means a problem to solve or a difficulty, and also a question on a test. The verb 문제를 풀다 means to solve, while 문제가 생기다 means a problem occurs.
mistakes: Saying 문제가 풀어요 instead of 문제를 풀어요

examples: There is a reason I am late.
I came without a special reason.
nuance: 이유 means the reason or cause behind something. Koreans ask 무슨 이유로 to mean for what reason, and 이유가 있다 means there is a reason.
mistakes: Saying 이유가 말해요 instead of 이유를 말해요

examples: I look for a new method.
nuance: 방법 means a method, way, or means of doing something. Koreans say 방법을 찾다 to find a way, and 방법으로 to mean by a certain method.
mistakes: Saying 방법이 찾아요 instead of 방법을 찾아요

examples: I have a special plan this evening.
I do not have weekend plans yet.
nuance: 계획 means a plan you make for the future. The natural verb is 계획을 세우다 meaning to set up a plan, not 계획을 만들다.
mistakes: Saying 계획을 만들어요 instead of 계획을 세워요

examples: I have plans with a friend tonight.
nuance: 약속 means both a promise and a social appointment to meet someone. The verb 약속을 지키다 means to keep a promise, and 약속이 있다 often means having plans.
mistakes: Saying 약속이 지켜요 instead of 약속을 지켜요

examples: I have a lot of work experience.
I had a good experience on the trip.
I want to have a new experience.
nuance: 경험 means experience, both the knowledge you gain and a single event you go through. With 하다 it becomes 경험하다, and 경험이 많다 means to be experienced.
mistakes: Saying 경험이 해요 instead of 경험을 해요
